restrictions: The two messages have 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 bytes for one t with 1 <= t < 2^32: t zero chunks of 1024 bytes followed by a last chunk of one block. The last chunk is compressed as a non-root chunk with counter t (v12 = t, v13 = 0), flags 3 and its true block length; the 63-byte block ends in eight zero bytes, so words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero in both zero-filled blocks. Equal last-chunk chaining values give equal digests by the tree lemma of proof.md Section 7.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every trial of proof.md Section 8 the two last-chunk chaining values agree on words 0, 2, 5 and 7, E1.c1 lies in the cube of beta* = 18b0e098 so that beta = beta* in every trial, Y4 ranges over the whole class of eta (524,288 values; no sub-class, no rule on h1), and the counter t is solved per trial as ROL(K0.d1,16) XOR K0.a1; trials with t = 0 are skipped. The search continues only in outer steps that pass the exact filter of proof.md Section 8 for the six listed E1 outcomes S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0 (share 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782); of these, the joint solver sees only those kept by the exact s-pattern pre-check, and its guards (G7) and (G15) drop only words that hold no success, so by Lemmas F, VP, G7 and G15 none of these steps loses a counted success. The eight other outcomes of beta* are not counted as successes.

Heuristic part: under H1', H4' and H5', each stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12, with probability at least 0.39 the search finds a trial whose remaining 128 chaining-value bits also agree. It walks 2^90.117 trials: 2^50.117 contexts (proof.md 9.8), each the seven outer words of one fresh draw, times the 2^19 members of the class, times the 2^21 trials of an outer step.

Machine: a classical word RAM with 256-bit words under collision-frontier-v5, 430 machine units (operations, loads, stores) to the unit, 64 registers and constants as immediates; fetching a word from memory is a load. Charges (proof.md 9.8, 9.9, 11; GPT Sol answers CD and CJ): 600 units per context, which draws its fresh word and runs the 39 member-free lines of step CO once; 66 units per partner batch of seven members in packed 36-bit lanes, its two list words adjacent (42 for the last batch of three partners of a cluster), which computes the 8 member lines on which omega depends and omega and tests every lane against the direct table T2; and 64 units for each lane whose test-(2) mask meets S, which updates the E count, held in a register, in three operations, computes the 17 lines on which only Y9 depends in 16 packed lines and tests against T1. The submitted program adds these charges per event and counts no machine operation.

Cluster gate (proof.md 9.9, Lemmas KP, A9, CL and OR; GPT Sol answers CI 1, CJ and CK 5): the 32 members that differ only in bits 10 to 14 of e1 form a cluster with omega mod 2^9 in two values computed from the representative; a fixed table P of 2^21 words skips the cluster when neither value can pass test (2), losing nothing. Charges: 74 units per batch of seven representatives (no T2 read; 56 for the last of a context; 2,341 per context) and 333 per opened cluster (partner batches 4 * 66 + 42, nesting 21 with the representative batch's seven words and the opened count in reserved registers, no memory frame, and the representative's T2, 6). The run halts when the opened count passes A_BUDGET = 9,189,056,937,678,035,781, and the time bound charges A_BUDGET + 1. No premise: Lemma OR proves that for uniform outer words the gate opens on at most 246,621,675 / 2^29 < 0.4593686667 of the clusters on average (a finite certificate, its check charged 2^34), and Hoeffding over contexts bounds the overflow by exp(-20).

Building T1 and T2, one entry per 32-bit word, costs below 2^39 units once (2^38 bytes). A passing lane is charged 494 units, its rebuild, the 37 words saved around the solver (the 29 of the batch and the 8 reserved registers), pre-check, the three words of (G7) and its credit test included. When the pre-check keeps outcomes T, the proved cap C15(T) <= 17,504 of the joint solver with the guards (G7) and (G15), its global ledger of 1,024 and the root certificates (four one-word tests, 120 units a root) is subtracted from a prepaid credit of 1,584,841,873,457,225,944,219 units before the solver starts. These are proved upper allowances of a specified layout, not measured counts. Nothing is sorted, every word-indexed read is charged as a load, and the tables do not grow with the trials.

Halts: the run stops with failure as soon as the opened-cluster count, the test-(2) count or the pass count passes its budget, as soon as a C15(T) is larger than the credit left, and after RUN_CONTEXTS = 1,220,926,580,812,448 contexts. E_BUDGET = 34,833,655,546,458,722,911 and PASS_BUDGET = 634,818,459,892,147,173 are the means at the factors of H4' plus 2^19 s, s = 110,495,547. The time bound charges each budget plus one, RUN_CONTEXTS + 1 contexts, all 2,341 * RUN_CONTEXTS representative batches and the whole credit, so it holds for every run (proof.md Sections 9, 11).

This package is our entry 415e792c with the member loop and the direct tables of entry e9b6649e (hecmas), the guard (G7) of our entry 0bc5f130 with the credit at the exact model mean with (G7), scaled by 16/27, the omega-first batch (GPT Sol, answer CA), the E count in a register, the root certificate, the guard (G15), the global ledger of 1,024 (answers CD and CF), the cluster gate with its layout (answers CI 1 and CJ), and the sharper opening bound, budget reserves and margins of answer CK. Randomness: one fresh uniform 256-bit word per context. Since each context visits each member of the class once or skips it in a cluster that fails test (2) (Lemmas CX and CL), means over outer steps equal those of a uniform outer step; independence holds between contexts only, so H1' (ii) is stated per context, which is stronger than a per-step clause. Success 0.39 holds only under H1', H4' and H5'.

The factor 125,920,632,087 in H1' is ten elevenths of the model's conditional count of the six listed outcomes on the class, rounded down: a declared margin of 11/10, supported by a preregistered 8-bit toy run of the counter arrangement (40,882 collisions found against 40,800.63 predicted), not proved. The organizer-run experiment does not measure it. The cluster gate, the filter, the pre-check, (G7) and (G15) lose nothing; the two count shares matter only for the budgets (H4') and the mean of C(T) with (G7) only for the credit (H5'). No full 2-round collision is exhibited.

The submitted program, experiments/frontline.py (proof.md 6.4), runs the search of proof.md 9.1 on the counter instance in each organizer trial: one fresh context, 32 of its clusters, the gate, test (2), the Q path, the filter, the pre-check, the credit test, the joint solver with (G7) and (G15), the root certificate and the halts, with every walked member checked against the full outer step. It adds the charges of Section 11 per event and does not model the machine layout; its halt constants are those at the rate factor 5/7, larger than the claim's, and no trial reaches them. The one thing it cannot show is the counter instance's digest: the organizer can hash only the root instance, so each trial returns the root-instance pair of its context (counter 0, flags 11), whose 128-bit half-collision the organizer recomputes. Its 16 observations are untrusted.

Fixed nonuniform advice, stated in full in proof.md Section 12: the six 32-bit constants of 3.2, eta = 830303cf, beta* = 18b0e098 with the mask 0e09818b and value 02008000 of its cube, the seven tau values and eps = 6e21be55 of the filter's automata and the mask 5f of S, 73 bytes in all (nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes 7). The success analysis uses only properties of this stated record that proof.md verifies exactly: Fact P (3.2), Lemma Q, Theorem C (iii) and (iv), the table of 10.1 with the program of Section 17, the certificate of the filter for S (Section 8), and the pre-check patterns and solver guards, trees and caps for this class (9.4, 9.7, 11). H1', H4' and H5' are stated for this record and none concerns how it was found; no premise concerns what any selection returns. The selection procedure SEL that found it is charged in full as preprocessing (preprocessing_log2).

preprocessing_log2 55, included in time_log2, is the charge of the selection procedure SEL of proof.md Section 12, which found the advice: 116 solver runs capped at 2^56 operations each, one count per model capped at 2^52 (+ 2^10), and the choice of S capped at 2^50, in all S_old = 8,882,224,365,081,579,520 operations, below 2^62.946, below 2^54.198 units, rounded up to 55. The cap holds by construction, since every run halts at its cap; that SEL returns exactly the stored values rests on the participant's solver log and recounts, which are not in the package. The cost model charges any search omitted from the submitted program; SEL is that search, and its whole capped cost is charged. The search alone is below 2^63.8999 units. memory_log2_bytes 44 covers, all held at once (sum below 2^44), the two output messages (each below 2^42 bytes), the search with its code and direct tables (below 2^39 bytes) and every run of SEL (below 2^34 + 2^20 bytes). No priority or novelty claim is made.

heuristics.statement: Score-critical. Stated for the instance that the advice record of proof.md Section 12 fixes, and for no other. The run has RUN_CONTEXTS independent contexts, each the seven outer words of one fresh uniform 256-bit word, and every context visits all 2^19 members of the class, except the members of clusters that the gate of proof.md 9.9 skips, which fail test (2) and hold no listed good trial (Lemmas CX and CL). Let N_o be the number of listed good valid trials of one outer step (t != 0, R = 0, and an E1 outcome in S = {175,185,275,285,385,685}020a0, six outcomes of beta*; Y4 in the whole class of eta; no rule on h1), counted over all of Q* whether or not the outer step passes the filter or the pre-check, and N_c its sum over the 2^19 outer steps of a context. (i) For a uniform outer step U (seven uniform outer words, a uniform member), E[N_o(U)] >= (2^21 - 1) q with q = FACTOR * 2^-128, FACTOR = floor(10 * 138,512,695,296 / 11) = 125,920,632,087, about 2^-91.126 (just under ten elevenths of the conditional model rate p of Lemma S1 for S); by Lemma CX (c), E[N_c] = 2^19 E[N_o(U)]. The margin 11/10 is a declared numerical clause, open (GPT Sol, answer CK 9); it is stronger than the factor 5/7 of entry 415e792c, which does not imply it. (ii) With the context as the unit, as entry e9b6649e declares it: the probability that no valid trial of the run is a listed good trial is at most exp(-0.49676) + 0.001; that is, listed good trials are not clustered, neither among the trials of one outer step nor among the outer steps (members) of one context, beyond what this bound allows. Given (i), rho_c = E[N_c(N_c-1)]/E[N_c] <= 0.0065 is sufficient for (ii) by Lemma S8 applied to the independent contexts. rho_c = rho_w + rho_x, where rho_w is the per-step factorial ratio of entry 415e792c and rho_x >= 0 the part that pairs of different members of one context add, so this clause is stronger than the per-step clause of entry 415e792c. Part (ii) is an assumption: rho_c is not measured and cannot be measured at full size (proof.md 10.3). This restates the rate-and-dependence premise of entry 26ebba63 for the whole class, S and the walk by contexts; that entry's clause was for the sub-class with rule A and seven outcomes and does not by itself imply this law (GPT Sol, answer AT 2). By Lemma F every listed good trial lies in an outer step that passes the filter, by Lemma CL the cluster gate skips none, by Lemma VP the pre-check skips none and by Lemmas G7 and G15 the guards (G7) and (G15) drop none, so N_o is the same count, pointwise (GPT Sol, answer AW 1).
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Sections 8 and 9: lengths 1024t + 55 and 1024t + 63 with a non-root last chunk (counter t, v13 = 0, flags 3), the six constants of Section 3.2, Y4 ranging over all 524,288 members of the class of eta (Lemma Q) inside every context, a context being the seven outer words of one fresh 256-bit word of the run (proof.md 9.8, Lemma CX); in every trial E1.c1 is drawn from the cube of beta* = 18b0e098, and t is solved per trial, with t = 0 skipped. The search continues only in outer steps that pass the exact filter of Section 8 for S, the solver sees only those that the pre-check of 9.7 keeps, and it applies the guards (G7) and (G15); N_o counts all of Q* in every outer step and only the six outcomes of S.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the participant's exact count, in integer arithmetic under the seven-word model of Section 10 with Y4 uniform in the class, of the part of beta* on the class carried by the six outcomes of S (67,633,152 = 1,032 * 2^16 on the per-trial scale 2^-83 of the class; the counting program and its output are printed in Section 17), times 2^11 for drawing E1.c1 from the cube (Lemma S1), taken at ten elevenths, rounded down. The margin 11/10: a preregistered 8-bit toy run of the counter arrangement (proof.md Section 13; PREREG.txt SHA-256 c5895dd64b07710f9fb386b0f9d4f6b5cb38b14b502a4cc80e51c60584432a4e) found 40,882 collisions of complete messages against 40,800.63 predicted, ratio 1.00199 +- 0.00496, one-sided 97.7 per cent lower bound 0.99213 >= 1/1.1, SUPPORTED; an earlier run of the same toy found 251 against 255.0. Participant evidence of Section 13, untrusted by the harness: a whole-class graphics-card run of 2^46 real counter trials, in which the E1 rate on the whole class of the seven outcomes of entry 59f8915e is 1.0020 +- 0.0086 of the model (13,595 events); the E1 event of S is a sub-event of it (52/53 in the model). At 32 bits the joint 128-bit event, about 2^-91 per trial, is not measured. Dependence: part (ii) is assumed. Under the model E[N_c] is about 2^-51.126, and rho_x is about v * E[N_c], where v is the clustering ratio of listed good trials by context (1 for independent members); so (ii) fails only if v exceeds about 2^43.9, or if one listed good trial makes another in the same context far more likely than its rate. Evidence that v is near 1: the same ratio, (E[n(n-1)]/E[n]) / ((2^19 - 1) p_hat) for per-context counts of events that every listed good trial meets, is 1.1513 for the filter pass, 1.1572 for the pass with the pre-check and 1.153 for an outer step whose solver reaches a leaf (120,000 contexts; control arms 1.0000, 1.0000 and 0.998), and 1.2486 +- 0.0806 for an outer step whose solver returns a root (46,104,576 contexts; control 1.0367 +- 0.0718). Preregistered (262,144 contexts and 2^46 trials per arm, two generators, a control arm): the cross-member factor Rx is 0.999 +- 0.054 (upper limit 1.162) for the listed E1 outcome, 2^-32.29 per trial, 0.90 +- 0.24 (upper limit 1.94) for (J1) and (J2) of the E3 half, 2^-34.58, and 1.0002 for R24; only the filter events cluster (1.144, 1.152); every upper limit lies at least 42 bits below the 2^43.86 that the clause allows.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 125,920,632,087 is assumed (ten elevenths of the model count of the six outcomes of S on the class, rounded down); its margin 11/10 rests on 8-bit toy evidence, not on a 32-bit transfer. The premise of entry 26ebba63 was for the sub-class with rule A; it is not inherited, and the whole-class law of N_o for S is declared, not proved. The organizer-run experiment walks one context of the counter search per trial but returns a root-instance pair (counter 0, flags 11); it measures neither the factor nor the counter half-collision, which the organizer cannot hash. Part of the transfer of the single-trial law to the actual sampler is proved (Lemmas S1-S5, S8, S9, VP, G7 and G15) and part is assumed in (i). Part (ii) is an assumption: the bound rho_c <= 0.0065 is not measured and cannot be measured at full size, since a context holds a listed good trial with probability about 2^-51.126; the proved cap of 16 listed good trials in one outer step does not help at this run length. Stated for contexts, it is stronger than a per-step clause. The clustering ratios that support it are measured for events that every listed good trial meets, not for listed good trials: the joint event, about 2^-91 per trial, is not reachable, so carrying Rx near 1 to it remains the premise. Lemmas F, VP, G7, G15 and S9 (a) use no law of the words.

heuristics.statement: Supporting; stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12. Two declared numerical clauses on means, open and not proved (GPT Sol, answer CK 2.1), for a uniform outer step U (seven uniform outer words, a uniform member): (a) the probability that U passes the filter for S is at most alpha_P pi, with alpha_P = 1.000176 and pi = 279,070,422,111 / 2^48 = 2^-9.9782; (b) the probability that its test-(2) mask meets S is at most alpha_E p_E, with alpha_E = 1.000026 and p_E = 233,715,456 / 2^32 = 2^-4.1998. Both are stronger than the factor 1.06 of entry 415e792c, which does not imply them. Use (proved): the pass count N_2 and the test-(2) count N_E add up independent per-context counts, each between 0 and 2^19, whose means are 2^19 times the probabilities for U (Lemma CX); PASS_BUDGET = ceil(alpha_P RUN_STEPS pi) + 2^19 s = 634,818,459,892,147,173 and E_BUDGET = ceil(alpha_E RUN_STEPS p_E) + 2^19 s = 34,833,655,546,458,722,911, with RUN_STEPS = 640,117,155,200,996,737,024 = 2^19 * RUN_CONTEXTS and s = ceil(sqrt(10 RUN_CONTEXTS)) = 110,495,547, so Hoeffding's inequality over the contexts bounds each overflow by exp(-2 s^2 / RUN_CONTEXTS) <= exp(-20). Reaching a budget halts with failure; the time bound charges each budget plus one. The number of outer steps that reach the solver has no budget here: the solver is paid from the credit of H5prime-weighted-solver-work (GPT Sol, answer AW 5).
heuristics.scope: The counts N_E and N_2 of proof.md 10.3, taken over all RUN_STEPS outer steps, every member of every context (9.1, 9.8): per context, each count lies between 0 and 2^19, the contexts are independent, and the mean per context is 2^19 times the indicator's probability for a uniform outer step (Lemma CX (c)); the two indicators of one outer step may depend on each other in any way.
heuristics.extrapolation: The nominal shares are exact for uniform independent (Y9, omega) (GPT Sol, answers AC, AN and AW 3; the certificate of Section 8). The two factors are the least, on a grid of one part per million, that pass a one-sided Chernoff test at confidence 1 - exp(-7) on the participant's preregistered sample of proof.md Section 13 (PREREG.txt SHA-256 92d16cda1cd13aacb287470b968ff2d914362b12fefb680c94960280a7471131), which counted both indicators exactly on 2^39 = 549,755,813,888 real outer steps of the whole class: 29,915,698,553 lanes with a nonzero test-(2) mask against the nominal 29,915,578,368, and 545,067,537 passing outer steps against 545,059,418.2; 1.000025 and 1.000175 fail the test (GPT Sol, answer CK 2.1, recomputed by the participant). Also measured, untrusted by the harness: a preregistered run of 262,144 contexts per arm gave the test-(2) and pass counts at 1.0000 +- 0.0008 and 1.0002 +- 0.0008 of nominal; with the member loop over 120,000 contexts the pass share was 0.99847 and the test-(2) share 0.99868 of nominal; on 60,000,000 real outer steps the counts were 1.0004 +- 0.0005 and 0.9980 +- 0.0041 of nominal.
heuristics.limitations: The two factors are not proved: Y9 and omega are not proved independent and uniform. The test reads the sample as ideal independent draws; its words come from a pseudorandom generator (Philox4x32-10). The factors are set at the least values that this sample supports, and the reserve 2^19 s is only 1.7 parts per million of E_BUDGET and 91 of PASS_BUDGET, so a physical share above its declared factor by more than about that would reach the budget and halt the run with failure, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound. The time bound, the filter and the pre-check do not depend on these shares.

heuristics.statement: Supporting; stated for the advice record of proof.md Section 12. This is the premise H4-AS-v-S(eps) of GPT Sol's answer AW 5, E_phys[V_S(U)] <= (1+eps) * cbar_S, taken at eps = 0.01 (answer CK 2.1) for the caps with the guard (G7) of answer AX 1: a declared numerical clause, open and not proved, stronger than the eps = 0.06 of entry 415e792c, which does not imply it. For an outer step U of the run, before any halt, let V(U) = C(T(U)), where T = X AND VMASK[nu] is the set of outcomes that the pre-check of proof.md 9.7 keeps and C is the proved (G7) cap of steps 2 and 3 on those outcomes (4,096 + 2,304 F + 1,280 A + 20 N_f + 48 N_r + 4 N_s + 368 Lf over the rows of T with their trees with (G7), Section 11; at most 31,456), with V(U) = 0 when T is empty or the step does not pass the filter; V(U) is at least 27/16 times the cap C15(T) that the run debits (guard (G15), the root certificate and the global ledger, Section 11). Premise: for a uniform outer step, and hence for the mean over the outer steps of one context (Lemma CX (c)), E[V(U)] <= 1.01 * cbar, where cbar = 582,173,006,981,436 / 2^47 = 4.136588... is the exact mean of V in the counting model. It is a single weighted moment over all outer steps, the zeros counted, and not a mean of executed work. Use (proved): the run debits C15(T) <= 16/27 C(T) before steps 2 and 3 from a credit that starts at CREDIT = m_C + ceil(sqrt(40 L_C m_C)) + 14 L_C = 1,584,841,873,457,225,944,219, with m_C = ceil(1.01 * 16/27 * RUN_STEPS * cbar) = 1,584,817,753,552,722,787,165 and L_C = 17,504 * 2^19, and halts with failure when C15(T) exceeds what is left; the per-context sums of C15(T) are independent and lie between 0 and L_C, so Bernstein's inequality over contexts puts the probability that the credit is exhausted at most exp(-20). The time bound charges the whole credit whether or not the premise holds; success 0.39 holds under H1', H4' and this premise (proof.md 10.3, 10.4).
heuristics.scope: V(U) for every one of the RUN_STEPS outer steps of proof.md 9.1, that is, for every member of every one of the RUN_CONTEXTS contexts (9.8), as a function of the context's outer words and the member, with S = 0x5f, the masks X of the filter of Section 8, nu by formula (V) of 9.7 and the caps with (G7) of Section 11; the mean is over all outer steps, passing or not.
heuristics.extrapolation: cbar is exact in the counting model M_v of proof.md 10.3 (uniform independent (Y9, omega) and an independent uniform three-bit nu): CBAR = 582,173,006,981,436 is an eighth of the sum of n_X C(X) over the ten masks X of S that occur, 4,657,384,055,851,488, recounted by the participant in integers from the certificate of Section 8 and the trees with (G7). Measured, untrusted by the harness: the participant's preregistered sample (PREREG.txt SHA-256 92d16cda1cd13aacb287470b968ff2d914362b12fefb680c94960280a7471131) of 2^39 = 549,755,813,888 real outer steps of the whole class measured V with (G7): mean 4.136407 against 4.136588, ratio 0.999956 +- 0.000089, one-sided upper bounds 1.000297 (empirical Bernstein, delta 0.00135, range 31,456) and 1.000384 (bounded KL), both below 1.01, so the rule fixed in advance (SUPPORTED at eps when the upper bound is at most 1 + eps) gives SUPPORTED at eps = 0.01. An earlier preregistered sample of 2^28 real outer steps, of V without (G7) and with another generator, bounds the mean with (G7) by 1.0786 times cbar through the pointwise ratio 723/715, which does not reach 1.01.
heuristics.limitations: Not proved: the sampler's nu is a function of the outer step and is not proved uniform or independent of the masks, so cbar is not a property of the sampler. Support at eps = 0.01 rests on the model value and on one preregistered sample from one pseudorandom generator (Philox4x32-10), run by the participant outside the organizer's harness; V is the proved cap C(T), not executed work, and the sample tests neither H1' nor the rate of H4'. If the premise fails, the credit can halt the run with failure, which lowers the success probability and not the time bound. This premise takes the place of the third count budget of our entry 0bc5f130.
